ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.as_written: the 1.662 headline is 'absent from both cited deposits and sits uncited in METRIC_r255.json'
ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.what_is_TRUE: The manuscript did lack a container citation for its designated headline number. That part stands and is now fixed.
ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.what_is_FALSE_1: It sits in TWO deposits, not one: METRIC_r255.json (two paths) and METRIC_LADDER_r256.json (one path). Three storage sites, all holding 1.6617781411076797 and agreeing to the last digit.
ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.what_is_FALSE_2: The things the manuscript cited are NOT deposits. PREREG_channels_G2_r219.md and PREREG_window_r218.md are REGISTRATIONS. Saying the value is 'absent from both cited deposits' miscategorises them: a registration states what WILL be measured and cannot carry a measured value. The citation pointed at the wrong KIND of file, which is a different defect from pointing at the wrong file.
ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.TWO_RESOLVERS_WERE_REQUIRED: A string grep for '1.662' finds the value NOWHERE -- it serialises as 1.6617781411076797. A naive numeric scan at three decimals returns FOUR files, adding PHASE_r258.json (lumbar_bending, pelvis_rotation, knee_angle_l) and VIDEO_DEGRADATION_POSTHOC.json (margin_gap_sd), all coincidental near-1.662 values on unrelated quantities and all distinguishable at full precision. Neither resolver alone answers the question -- the r349 taxonomy in live form.
ROUND4_DEFECT16_HALF_FALSE_r350.registrations_retained: The registration citations were KEPT in the manuscript. They are correct as statements of what was pre-specified; they are simply not the source of the value.
